eyebrow: A different question than scope mechanics
code:
Scripting & Application Development:     This lesson:
- HOW one scoped app isolates itself      - HOW MANY scoped apps should an
  (sys_scope, naming, access)                instance actually have
- mechanics of one application            - where the boundaries between
                                               them should fall
caption: Isolation mechanics vs. the enterprise question of scope boundaries.

code:
Too many narrow scopes:                Too few broad scopes:
- more upgrade-testing efforts         - one bug's blast radius covers
- more cross-scope access to manage       every unrelated bundled feature
- splits with no real org boundary     - no team releases independently
caption: Both failure modes are real — the fix isn't "more" or "fewer," it's the right boundary.

code:
Ask: does one team build, test, and
deploy this independently of another?

  Same team, same release cadence  ->  probably one scope
  Separate team, own release calendar -> probably its own scope
caption: Functional and ownership lines, not naming convenience, decide the edge.
